papers.title: Semiampleness of Hodge line bundles and b-semiampleness of the moduli part
papers.abstract: We give proofs of Hodge semiampleness and b-semiampleness without using o-minimality. We establish a geometric semiampleness criterion for line bundles on proper algebraic spaces. Let $(X,D)$ be a log smooth pair with $X$ a proper algebraic space. For an integral polarizable pure variation of Calabi--Yau type on $X\setminus D$ with unipotent local monodromy, let $L$ be its extended highest Hodge line. If $L$ is numerically integrable and has torsion combinatorial monodromy, then $L$ is semiample. We also prove semiampleness of extended Griffiths lines. We construct normal projective period compactifications on which a positive power of the Griffiths line extends to an ample line bundle. As an application, we prove that the moduli b-divisor $\mathbf{M}$ of a projective lc-trivial fibration over a normal algebraic variety is b-semiample, provided that the generic boundary is effective. Suppose further that the geometric generic pair is klt and its boundary is big, with nonzero coefficients in a fixed finite set $I\subset(0,1)\cap\mathbb{Q}$. Then $c\mathbf{M}$ is b-Cartier and b-free for an integer $c>0$ depending only on the relative dimension and $I$. We extend b-semiampleness to analogous projective fibrations over normal complex analytic bases, assuming a global relative polarization and an invertible log pluricanonical sheaf pulled back from the base.

papers.title: $λ_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
papers.abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $λ_gψ^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

papers.title: On sinks and mirrors
papers.abstract: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichmüller and moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichmüller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

papers.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
papers.abstract: The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold. We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.

papers.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.
authors: with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane developed by Haiman.

papers.title: Multi-monopoles and monodromy around the wobbly divisor
papers.abstract: The multi-monopole equations are a generalisation of the Seiberg--Witten equations where the spinor is coupled to an auxiliary vector bundle. The signed count of multi-monopoles on a 3-manifold can vary according to a new type of wall-crossing phenomenon. For products $S^1\times C$, where $C$ is a closed Riemann surface, we relate the wall and chamber structure to loops in the complement of the wobbly divisor of $C$. Such a loop induces a monodromy map on the multi-vortex moduli space, and the count of its fixed points is expected to agree with the count of multi-monopoles on $S^1\times C$ in the given chamber. By studying singularities of framed multi-vortex moduli spaces, we are able to understand these monodromy maps for various loops. Counting fixed points suggests that product 3-manifolds display incredibly rich wall-crossing behaviour.

papers.title: Kappa Classes on the KSBA Space of Stable Toric Pairs
papers.abstract: We study kappa classes on the normalization of the main component of the Kollár--Shepherd-Barron--Alexeev(KSBA) moduli space of stable toric pairs. Using a toric model obtained by a lattice modification, we compute all kappa classes on the moduli space by giving a combinatorial formula for their intersection numbers with all torus-invariant cycles. In particular, we identify the first normalized kappa class with the GKZ polarization of the toric variety corresponding to the secondary polytope. For interval configurations, we also obtain a closed formula for all top intersection products of normalized kappa classes.

papers.title: The Chow ring of a wonderful compactification
papers.abstract: The theory of wonderful compactifications provides a common framework encompassing the constructions of important varieties such as the Fulton-MacPherson configuration spaces, the moduli space of $n$-pointed stable rational curves, and the De Concini-Procesi models of subspace arrangements, and, more generally, of smooth compactifications in which the subvarieties in a building set are replaced by a simple normal crossings boundary divisor. We give a presentation of the Chow ring of a wonderful compactification, assuming only that the Chow ring of the ambient variety surjects onto that of each subvariety in the induced arrangement. Our results recover and extend many previously known presentations and apply to a broad range of new examples.

papers.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
papers.abstract: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(μ)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(μ)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $Φ(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).

papers.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
papers.abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\CH(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\CH(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $λ_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(λ_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.
